claim: For every infinite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space \(H\) and every nonzero Banach space \(X\), there is a sequence of rank-one operators \(R_n\in S_{\mathcal K(H,X)}\) such that \(\sup\{\inf_{n\ge1}\|S+R_n\|:S\in\mathcal K(H,X),\ \|S\|\le1\}=\sqrt{2}\). Thus this fixed countable family witnesses failure of \(\omega_1\)-octahedrality of \(\mathcal K(H,X)\) with exact gap \(2-\sqrt{2}\).

integrity.provenance_note: The exact estimate is derived in the included proof; the cited 2026 source provides the qualitative context.

scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns infinite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert domains and compact operators only.
The exact minimax value is for the explicit orthonormal rank-one sequence in the claim, not an optimization over all possible witness sequences.
No classification for arbitrary uniformly convex Banach domains or noncompact perturbations is claimed.
title: A sharp \(\sqrt{2}\) obstruction for compact operators with Hilbert domain
